q1_issues.issue: The exhaustive "all" of "which is all oral examination" is silently dropped, leaving the unqualified (Member sk_round_1 oral_examination) rather than carrying the qualifier or leaving the claim out and recording the gap.

q2_gaps: exhaustive / wholly "all" modifying a predicate nominal ("the round is all oral examination") — no licensed carrier: QuantifierPhrase's <subject> <predicate> "<word>" shape is for quantified subject sets, not a mass-exhaustiveness reading of the complement

a time-denoting genitive possessor ("today's third round") — the possessive/genitive rule offers exactly one test (part-component vs Possession) and has no branch for a deictic time as possessor; the parse's (Time sk_round_1 today) is licensed only by analogy to the event-noun Time rule, not by the genitive rule itself

Ordinal's scale slot for a non-event ordinal ("the third round") — the instruction set defines the slot as the associated event or an explicit "-est" dimension, and a position in a sequence of rounds supplies neither
notes: The group + Cardinality 2 for "both", the per-member distribution rule beside the group event, the preposition-named In for "in ... round", and the oral_examination genus/modifier decomposition all follow the instruction set. The antecedentless "Both" is typed person, which the pronoun rule permits only on discourse evidence of a human-only predicate or role — "compete in an oral examination" is suggestive but is not itself such a role.
